text:
maria: quick thread — hit a weird regression in prod where a session observed a stale prefix blob after we evicted and rebalanced tenants.
ben: logs?
maria: pasted minimal repro (timestamps trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] tenant=acme prefix=/chat/conv123 prefix_version=42 served_from_cache
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] reassign host for tenant=acme seq=17 -> 18
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] eviction triggered pool-7 removed /chat/conv123 (version=42)
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] replica-sync applied blob (version=41) to pool-7
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] tenant request saw prefix_version=41 (stale)
```
sangeeta: hmm — looks like a race between eviction/replica sync and sequencer reassignment. are we using any monotonic tag on cache entries today?
kevin: we currently store a lease token + last-updated timestamp. nothing globally monotonic per-tenant.
maria: exactly. during leader change the sequencer's canonical version moves forward but a lagging replica can re-fill cache with older blobs.
jamal: high-level fixes: 1) strong lease/centralized fill gate (sequencer mediates fills). 2) attach sequencer epoch to entries and reject lower epochs on fill. 3) validate-first-on-serve (serve then verify for first N requests). tradeoffs?
ben: 1) has availability & latency hit — every fill touches sequencer. 2) epoch tag seems cheap: just compare local entry. 3) validation-first is pragmatic but still risks brief incorrect responses.
sangeeta: also think about shared pools: eviction is pool-wide, but epoch is tenant-scoped. pool workers need to be tenant-aware on accept.
maria: proposal: sequencer maintains tenant_epoch (increment on leader switch or when we bump model state). cache entries include tenant_epoch in metadata. on cache fill, worker compares incoming_blob.epoch >= current_known_epoch for tenant — if older, reject and trigger fresh fetch from origin (sequencer or primary store).
kevin: where does worker get current_known_epoch? local small cache of tenant -> epoch refreshed from sequencer; fetch on miss. cost of fetch? microsecond? more like a small RPC.
jamal: failure modes: transient extra latency for first post-switch requests. what about cross-region? sequencer epoch must be globally consistent per-tenant.maria: yep — sequencer already has global lease manager per-tenant; exposing a tenant_epoch endpoint is trivial. implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
// on sequencer leader change
tenant_epoch[tenant] += 1
// on cache worker fill
if blob.epoch < local_epoch_for(tenant): reject_fill()
else accept()
```
ben: does this prevent a stale blob that legitimately has a higher epoch but older content? epoch only demonstrates ordering of state changes, not content correctness.
sangeeta: true. epoch is a conservative guard to avoid regressions due to leader reassign. content regressions need eval / checksums. we can also include content-hash and sequencer-issued fill-token for stronger guarantees.
kevin: storage overhead: entry now has epoch (8 bytes) + optional token (uuid). acceptable vs complexity of central fill.
jamal: operationally, what about the eviction algo — should we prefer removing low-epoch entries first during pool rebalance? maybe a 'soft quarantine' window where entries with epoch < current are deprioritized for serving until validated.
maria: I threw together a perf run: epoch-guarding increases p95 for cold-first-request by ~3% but reduces correctness incidents to 0 in our 1000-switch sim. cheaper than serialized fills through sequencer.
ben: sounds promising. can you paste the perf snippet and the minimal code we need to add to pool worker?
maria: pasted short diff idea: 
```
struct CacheEntry { bytes value; uint64 epoch; }
onFill(blob) {
  if (blob.epoch < tenantEpochCache.get(blob.tenant)) return ERR_STALE;
  insert(entry)
}
```
sangeeta: operational flags: add feature-flag rollout + metrics: epoch_mismatch_count, rejected_fills, extra_fetch_latency.
kv-bot: eviction-scan completed pool-7 removed=234 epoch_mismatch_rate=0.8% last_scan=2026-03-18T09:14:00Z
kevin: next steps — RFC this as 'tenant-epoch cache guard' + rollout plan (feature flag, metrics, perf tests). owners?
maria: I'll draft RFC + perf artifact, ping eng-platform for tenant-epoch endpoint. I'll own worker patch and rollout plan. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-platform.
ben: thanks — can we also sketch fallback: on rejected fill, do synchronous fetch then warm cache to avoid client fail? lowers visible errors.
maria: yes will include that — synchronous fill + exponential backoff for retries.
jamal: +1 on RFC. let's avoid centralizing every fill.
sangeeta: agree. add QA test that simulates leader switch + replica sync to catch regressions.
maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
